% Converted, ltx-talk. The frame headers are exactly what
% scripts/fix_frame_titles.py emits from before.tex (verified by running it: "2
% frame title(s) fixed") -- a real brace matcher, run AFTER convert_deck.py,
% which is the documented workaround for C-FRAMETITLE-NESTED. The double form is
% joined with " --- ".
%
% The one hand edit is \sc -> \scshape. fix_frame_titles.py preserves \sc
% verbatim (correctly -- old font commands are convert_deck.py's job), but \sc is
% undefined under ltx-talk, so the folded title fails to compile until C-OLDFONT
% is applied too. Confirmed: leaving \sc in gives exit 1 and one "Undefined
% control sequence". These two compromises have to be fixed together, and a
% nested title is exactly where one hides the other.
\DocumentMetadata{lang=en, pdfversion=2.0, pdfstandard=a-4, tagging=on}
\documentclass{ltx-talk}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}[c]
\frametitle{\only<1>{Example}\only<2>{Find a plan for}}
Single braced title, nested.
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}[c]
\frametitle{Arc consistency --- {\scshape Inference}}
Double braced title, nested.
\end{frame}
\end{document}
